title: Transferred model structure on simplicial modules
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let $\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda$ be the category of functors from $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $\Lambda$-modules, with natural transformations [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Write $U:\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda\to\mathsf{sSet}$ for forgetting the module structure, where simplicial sets, horn inclusions, Kan fibrations and weak homotopy equivalences have the Kan model conventions of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Use model categories and Quillen adjunctions as defined in [lem-cbc-dg-presheaf-model-localizations]. Let $N(A)_0=A_0$ and $N(A)_n=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\ker(d_i)$ for $n>0$, with differential $d_0$. The category $\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda$ has a model structure in which weak equivalences and fibrations are created by $U$. Under the normalization equivalence [lem-cbc-dold-kan-normalization-equivalence], weak equivalences are precisely quasi-isomorphisms of nonnegative chains, and fibrations are precisely maps surjective in every strictly positive normalized degree, with no surjectivity requirement in degree zero. The degreewise free-module functor $\Lambda[-]:\mathsf{sSet}\to\mathsf{sMod}_\Lambda$ is left Quillen. In particular, for every weak homotopy equivalence $f$ of simplicial sets, $N\Lambda[f]$ is a quasi-isomorphism of nonnegative chain complexes.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, sequence (1) and the transferred simplicial-module/projective connective-chain model paragraph immediately before Proposition 3.15, printed pp. 11–12. The final consequence uses that every simplicial set is cofibrant in the Kan model.

proof.text: In each degree the free module on the underlying set is left adjoint to the forgetful functor. Applying this degreewise and using the functoriality of the face and degeneracy maps gives an adjunction $\Lambda[-]\dashv U$ between simplicial sets and simplicial $\Lambda$-modules: a simplicial linear map is uniquely determined by the images of the basis simplices, and the simplicial identities make these assignments natural.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, sequence (1), printed p. 11; degreewise free-module/forgetful adjunction.

proof.text: Let $T_\Lambda$ be the one-sorted Lawvere theory of $\Lambda$-modules: its objects are finite powers of one sort and its morphisms are $\Lambda$-linear matrix maps. It is small, and product-preserving functors $T_\Lambda\to\mathsf{sSet}$ are exactly simplicial $\Lambda$-modules; evaluation at the distinguished sort is the underlying simplicial-set functor $U$, and the free functor $F_*$ is $\Lambda[-]$. The boundary and horn generating maps in [lem-coef-sorted-simplicial-algebra-model] therefore become $\Lambda[\partial\Delta^n]\to\Lambda[\Delta^n]$ and $\Lambda[\Lambda_i^n]\to\Lambda[\Delta^n]$. Applying that transferred model theorem supplies a model structure with weak equivalences and fibrations detected by $U$, including the two lifting systems and functorial factorizations.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, transferred simplicial-module model paragraph immediately before Proposition 3.15, printed pp. 11–12.

proof.text: By the free--forgetful adjunction of Step 1, $Uf$ lifts against a horn precisely when $f$ lifts against its degreewise free-module image. The Dold--Kan equivalence [lem-cbc-dold-kan-normalization-equivalence] then identifies these lifting squares and their fillers with those for $Nf$ against $i:N\Lambda[\Lambda_k^n]\to N\Lambda[\Delta^n]$. Here $n\geq1$ and $0\leq k\leq n$, including both outer horns.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, sequence (1) and transferred simplicial-module/projective connective-chain model paragraph before Proposition 3.15, printed pp. 11–12; normalized Moore horn calculation.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-normalized-horn-disk], $i$ is isomorphic, with its domain fixed, to the summand inclusion $K\to K\oplus D^n$, where $K=N\Lambda[\Lambda_k^n]$. By [lem-cbc-disk-lifting-surjective], $Nf$ lifts against this inclusion exactly when $(Nf)_n$ is surjective. Taking all horn dimensions gives precisely positive-degree normalized surjectivity; no horn has degree zero, so degree-zero surjectivity is not required.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, sequence (1) and transferred simplicial-module/projective connective-chain model paragraph before Proposition 3.15, printed pp. 11–12; normalized Moore horn calculation.

proof.text: The Moore comparison [lem-cbc-simplicial-module-moore-homotopy] identifies homotopy groups based at zero with normalized homology, and identifies components with $A_0/d_0N(A)_1$. Translation by a vertex $a$ is the simplicial automorphism $x\mapsto x+s(a)$, where $s(a)$ is its totally degenerate simplex; it takes zero to $a$ and commutes with a simplicial linear map after translating its target by $f(a)$. Thus the comparison applies at every vertex basepoint and, by change of basepoint along a path inside a realization component, at every basepoint. The definition of weak equivalence in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] now says exactly that all normalized homology maps, including degree zero, are isomorphisms. Hence transferred weak equivalences are precisely normalized quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, sequence (1) and transferred simplicial-module/projective connective-chain model paragraph before Proposition 3.15, printed pp. 11–12; normalized Moore horn calculation.

proof.text: The right adjoint $U$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations by construction, since both classes in the transferred model are created by $U$. By the stated definition of a Quillen adjunction, the free-module functor $\Lambda[-]$ is therefore left Quillen.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, transferred adjunction paragraph before Proposition 3.15, printed pp. 11–12.

proof.text: Every simplicial set is cofibrant in the Kan model because the initial inclusion is a monomorphism. The left-Quillen preservation clause of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] (Ken Brown's lemma) therefore sends a weak homotopy equivalence $f$ of simplicial sets to a weak equivalence $\Lambda[f]$ of simplicial modules. Applying the normalized weak-equivalence criterion established in Step 5, using [lem-cbc-dold-kan-normalization-equivalence] and [lem-cbc-simplicial-module-moore-homotopy], gives that $N\Lambda[f]$ is a quasi-isomorphism of nonnegative chain complexes, as claimed.

source.place: Choudhury–Gallauer, §3.3, final sentence of the transferred-model paragraph before Proposition 3.15, printed p. 12.
